intended_object: The primitive quadratic Dirichlet character of conductor 8 attached to ℚ(√-2)/ℚ, i.e. the Kronecker symbol n ↦ (-8/n). It sends odd n ≡ 1, 3 mod 8 to 1, odd n ≡ 5, 7 mod 8 to −1, and even n to 0. This comes from the docstring.
explanation: For an odd prime p, (-2/p) = 1 exactly when p ≡ 1 or 3 mod 8, and −1 when p ≡ 5 or 7 mod 8. The definition gives these values on the odd residues, and 0 on the even residues, which are the non-units of ZMod 8. So it is the multiplicative character (-8/·) on ZMod 8 with values in ℤ, as the docstring says. It is a specific object, so the question of greater generality does not arise. I found no other Mathlib definition of this particular character.
